channel.title: LOUD LOCAL
channel.description: San Jose culture. Loud opinions. A city worth showing up for.

item.title: Mythbusting: Cheaper Illicit Is the Same Flower
item.description: A lower black-market number is not a lab result. Taxes, testing, and unknown pesticides explain much of the gap, and SJPD cases show why source still matters.

item.title: Cannabis Journalism Ethics for a Local Shopper Paper
item.description: Deal calendars and enforcement posts can live in one paper if the ethics are explicit: verify, disclose, refuse fake balance, and protect readers from harm.

item.title: Spanish-Language Shopping Confidence: Asking for Help at the Counter
item.description: San Jose’s bilingual everyday life should extend to cannabis retail. You can ask for Spanish help, plain explanations, and label clarity without apology.

item.title: East San Jose Gambling Raid: Illicit Cannabis in Crime Scenes vs. Licensed Retail
item.description: SJPD’s Sept. 16 seizure paired illegal gaming machines with about 13 pounds of marijuana. For licensed shoppers, the lesson is supply-chain clarity, not panic.

item.title: Faith Communities and Cannabis: Local Tone Without Stereotype
item.description: South Bay congregations span abstinence teachings, harm-reduction pastoral care, and quiet don’t-ask cultures. Shoppers deserve nuance, not caricature.

item.title: Workplace Drug Testing in the South Bay After Off-Duty Legal Use
item.description: California legalized adult use; many employers still test. Tech, warehouse, healthcare, and federal-contract workers need clear-eyed habits, not forum myths.

item.title: FEATURE: Purple Lotus Downtown NFL Block Party, Community Kickoff Energy on West Santa Clara
item.description: Purple Lotus’s downtown NFL Block Party put food, a DJ, and brand booths at 66 W Santa Clara St. for Sept. 12. Read the ticket math and public-consumption limits before you treat it like a free sidewalk sale.

item.title: Parking Reality: Industrial Corridors vs. Downtown Cannabis Retail
item.description: Where San Jose allows cannabis storefronts shapes the parking hunt. Industrial edges trade walkability for lots; downtown trades lots for meters, garages, and patience.

item.title: VTA Light-Rail Days: Carrying Sealed Cannabis Discreetly and Legally
item.description: Transit-friendly shopping is possible when products stay sealed, odor-controlled, and unconsumed on platforms and trains.

item.title: Tourism Day Map: Downtown Plazas and Legal Purchase Timing (Neutral Guide)
item.description: Visitors can walk plazas, museums, and transit, and still make a lawful cannabis purchase, if they time ID checks, sealed transport, and private consumption correctly.

item.title: Sustainability: Packaging Waste and California’s Cannabis Trash Problem
item.description: Child-resistant tubes and multilayer pouches protect kids, and fill trash cans. South Bay shoppers can reduce waste without pretending regulation is optional.

item.title: Fake Shops and Instagram Menus: Red Flags for San Jose Shoppers
item.description: Polished reels and DM menus are not city registration. A short checklist keeps South Bay adults on the lawful side of scarce storefronts.

item.title: Western Division Stop: Marijuana, Ghost Guns, and Knowing Your Source
item.description: An Aug. 24 SJPD vehicle stop that bundled smoked cannabis, sales indicia, and illegally built firearms is a youth-and-safety story licensed shoppers can use without the lecture.

item.title: Women, Queer, and BIPOC Shoppers: Finding Respectful Rooms
item.description: Respect is a service standard, not a niche marketing slogan. Shoppers can spot it without needing a guided tour of any one store.

item.title: 420 Season in San Jose: What Changed After Downtown Park Festivals
item.description: April 2026 put a ticketed 420 weekend on the plaza calendar. The lasting change is cultural visibility, not a rewrite of public-use law.

item.title: Music in the Park, Plaza Culture, and Cannabis Norms
item.description: Plaza de César Chávez is downtown’s living room. Cannabis culture may appear on festival posters, public consumption still generally may not.

item.title: Concert Nights Downtown: Plan the Purchase Before the Show
item.description: Downtown shows reward timing. Buy legal earlier, keep product sealed, and do not treat plazas or sidewalks as green rooms.

item.title: Food Trucks at Cannabis Events: Eat, Don’t Consume On-Site
item.description: BBQ lines and DJ sets borrowed festival grammar for adult retail weekends. The food is the point outdoors, the cannabis waits for private property.

item.title: SJSU and Community-College Students: Discount Myths vs. ID Rules
item.description: Student discounts may exist as retailer promotions, age 21 adult-use ID rules do not bend for campus proximity.

item.title: Veterans and Cannabis in the South Bay: A Practical Non-Hype Guide
item.description: State-legal retail is open to adult veterans, VA benefits and federal employment rules are a different conversation.

item.title: SB 34 Compassion Donations: How Free Medicine Pathways Work
item.description: California’s Dennis Peron and Brownie Mary Act lets licensed retailers donate tested medicinal cannabis to qualifying patients, not recreational bargain hunters.

item.title: Banks, Jobs, and Gun Forms: Federal Law Still Shapes Local Life
item.description: A legal San Jose receipt does not rewrite HR policies, firearm forms, or federal banking friction.

item.title: Federal Schedule III Talk: What Adult-Use San Jose Shoppers Should (Not) Expect
item.description: Medical scheduling headlines are not a green light for every adult-use jar, and they do not replace SJPD registration.

item.title: Public Consumption: Plaza de César Chávez, Parks, and Downtown Sidewalks
item.description: California’s adult-use law did not turn downtown plazas into smoking lounges, public places remain off-limits.

item.title: Unincorporated Santa Clara County vs. City of San Jose Shopping
item.description: County commercial bans push many South Bay buyers into San Jose’s licensed storefronts, and city tax reality.

item.title: Measure U and San Jose’s Cannabis Business Tax, Why Prices Feel High
item.description: Voters authorized a local gross-receipts cannabis tax years before adult-use retail, and shoppers still feel it in shelf prices.

item.title: Ordinance 31273 in Plain English for Shoppers
item.description: The late-2025 code update did not reopen retail applications, but it did rewrite registration timing and delivery math.

item.title: Why San Jose Has So Few Cannabis Storefronts
item.description: Closed retail applications, a narrow equity on-ramp, and a roster near twenty registered businesses explain the empty corners.

item.title: What “Licensed” Actually Means in San Jose (City + State)
item.description: A state cannabis license and a San Jose Notice of Completed Registration are related, but not interchangeable.

item.title: How to Read SJPD’s Registered Cannabis List Before You Shop
item.description: The city’s public registry, not a deal flyer, is the map of who may lawfully sell or deliver cannabis in San Jose.
